# QA Plan: Sprint 2 (Production Foundation and Core spine)
**Date**: 2026-10-25 (generated; sprint runs 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-20)
**Generated by**: /qa-plan sprint (unattended, autonomous mode, `qa.level: full`, `workflow: full`)
**Scope**: 219 story rows across 8 systems: 218 schedulable (86 Must, 54 Should, 78 Nice to Have) plus 1 blocked (CAM-011). Systems: TDC 77, PSR 33, RMF 39, IIF 29, SCL 12, ST 25, IVP 2, CPA 1, CAM 1. No story file was missing.
**Engine**: Unreal Engine 5.8 (installed 5.8.4)
**Sprint File**: `production/sprints/sprint-02.md` (status source: `production/sprint-status.yaml`; every one of the 219 rows is present in the yaml with `sprint: 2`)

> **Plan basis.** Story **Type** fields are accepted as declared (all 219 declare one; none inferred). Test names and test file paths come from each story's own `## Test Evidence` section and acceptance criterion; per-story test cases come from each story's `## QA Test Cases` section, which the qa-lead wrote at story creation. Where those cases exist this plan points at them and does not restate them ("do not invent test cases during implementation"). **33 stories have no QA Test Cases** (their section reads "Test cases not yet defined, run /qa-plan"): section "Test cases for stories that have none" below derives them strictly from each story's acceptance criterion and flags every ambiguity the story's QL-STORY-READY note already raised. No story file was edited (see decision D-1), no Status was touched, no code was touched.
>
> **Workflow tier.** `workflow: full` and no `system_overrides`, so all 8 GDD sections are in scope; edge-case and acceptance-criteria material was taken through the stories (which cite the GDD AC ids and Edge Cases they cover) rather than re-reading the eight 125-205 KB GDDs whole.

### Classification flags (type is never overridden; these are secondary types, gaps and risks)

- **No UI stories and one Visual/Feel story.** The sprint goal is logic, test and spike work; nothing is player-visible except through retained spike reports and harness result JSON. The only Visual/Feel row is **CPA-003** (retained UE viewport screenshot plus art-director sign-off, still pending AC-3). The player-observable evidence gate therefore applies to CPA-003, to **SCL-010** (Integration, but its Test Evidence requires a retained screenshot of a walking and a running pawn), to **SCL-006** (Integration, Nice; retained screenshot of a started round) and to **IVP-005** (lead-signed frame sequence). All four carry a screenshot row below at every `qa.level`.
- **Spike stories are Integration with a documented-measurement report as evidence.** IIF-008, 009, 010, 011; ST-001, 002, 003, 004; IVP-005, 006; TDC-071 (Nice); CAM-011 (blocked). A spike closes with PASS, FAIL plus fallback, or an amendment request; never by skipping. Reports are retained in `production/qa/spikes/`.
- **33 stories have no QA Test Cases** (15 Must, 6 Should, 11 Nice to Have, 1 blocked; see the section below): Must PSR-001, PSR-004, PSR-009, IIF-001, IIF-002, IIF-004, IIF-005, IIF-006, IIF-094, IIF-095, ST-006, ST-007, IIF-007, ST-001, ST-002; Should PSR-018, IIF-012, IIF-014, IIF-015, IIF-016, IIF-019; Nice PSR-021, PSR-027, PSR-029, PSR-031, PSR-033, IIF-020, IIF-021, IIF-022, IIF-024, IIF-026, ST-032; blocked CAM-011. 31 of them carry QL-STORY-READY **GAPS** and IIF-094 and IIF-095 are NOT ASSESSED (added after the review); the other 186 rows have qa-lead cases in their story files.
- **IIF-094 and IIF-095 are NOT ASSESSED** by QL-STORY-READY (added after the review) and their Type is Integration while sitting in the Must tier: they gate IIF-009 (V2 spike) and every IIF PIE story, so they get the earliest QA attention (readiness check before they enter a batch).
- **Logic stories that need a PIE or multi-process run despite the Logic label:** none identified; every Logic story names a headless automation test or a script selftest. **Integration stories with an "or documented playtest" alternative** (ST-001, ST-003, ST-004, ST-014, IIF-015, IIF-018, IIF-019, IIF-094): the alternative is accepted only when the machine window or hardware (second client, gamepad) is genuinely unavailable, and the documented playtest must be written with `/playtest-report` naming the story (decision D-3).
- **Status drift:** only CPA-003 is `In Progress` (Blender half done, UE import and AC-3 outstanding); all other rows are `Ready`. The plan does not change any Status.
- **Missing prerequisites that cap evidence (from the sprint plan, copied here because they limit what QA can accept):** no self-hosted runner (TDC-022/023 close on file text, real run DEFERRED); GitHub remote LFS lock behaviour unobserved (TDC-027 uses its stated fallback); no 3060-class reference machine (every performance or timing capture is labelled development evidence); S1 whole-pawn parity FAIL has no superseding ADR (S1-gated stories are not planned, so no QA is planned for them).

## Automated Tests Required

### Conventions that apply to every automated test in this sprint

- **Roots** (`.claude/docs/directory-structure.md`, Unreal row): tests live under `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/`; lint and CI selftests live under `tools/ci/**/selftest/` and are run with `python -I` (shell selftests with `bash`). Each story's Test Evidence names its exact file; this plan does not move any.
- **Names** (`.claude/rules/test-standards.md`, ADR-0008): `StealthGame.<System>.<Scenario>`, class `F<System><Scenario>Test`, one class per `IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST`, flags `EditorContext | ProductFilter`, file wrapped in `#if WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS`. CQTest network tests are `StealthGame.<System>.PIE.<Scenario>.<Method>`; Gauntlet nodes are `StealthGame.<System>.MP.<Scenario>`. The project filter is `^StealthGame.`.
- **Determinism** (`coding-standards.md`): injected clock (`IStealthClock`, RMF-001 fake clock), injected entropy and fixed server secrets (RMF-002, ST-009), no wall-clock pass predicate, no random seeds other than named constants, no shared mutable state, and **assert zero unexpected faults at teardown** (TDC-008 fault sink). Fixture literals live in constant files, not inline (RMF-005 is the static scan for this).
- **Negative controls.** Every lint or scan story (TDC-029 to 037, ST-012, ST-022, the SCL scans) must show its check failing on a planted violation before the pass is trusted (`test-standards.md`: a gate you have not watched fail is not a gate). TDC-035 is the sprint's explicit negative control for the doc lint; every other lint story records its planted-violation run in its completion notes.
- **Tiers.** T0 lint and script selftests run per commit without the editor; T1 headless automation runs under `-nullrhi`; T2 CQTest PIE (listen server plus clients) needs the single editor instance; T3 multi-process Gauntlet needs a cooked Development build and an exclusive machine window. T2 and T3 work cannot overlap a UBT build (single-lane constraint).
- **Forbidden patterns to guard** (from `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`; the ones a test in this sprint can cover):
  - Roster: server queries are O(1) and allocation-free; every client call returns `Rejected_NotAuthority` / `NotTargetable(Stale)` / false / 0 and reports to the fault sink (PSR-004, PSR-033).
  - Round: `Voided` limited to one per source per second; `KillResolved`, `Reversal`, `StateTransition`, `StrikeLimit`, `ObjectiveStage`, `FinalCompleted`, `WinLatched` never evicted; `Move`/`Look` never logged (RMF-011 to 015).
  - Tuning: invariant `Check` functions are pure; invariants reject or warn, never repair (TDC-048, 049, 055).
  - Input: no caller-identity parameter and no `IsPlayerControlled|IsLocallyControlled|IsNpc|GetTeam|NM_ListenServer` in the command component (IIF-006); no Hold/Tap/Pulse/HoldAndRelease/Chorded trigger on any server-meaning `IA_*` action and no `UPlayerMappableInputConfig` (IIF-007).
  - Session/RNG: no `FMath::Rand`, `FMath::FRand`, `FMath::RandRange`, `FRandomStream` in StealthFoundation or StealthGameplay (ST-012); reference and golden vectors use only `uint64`/`uint32` with defined wrap (ST-005, 006, 010).
  - Pillar 1: never branch on `IsPlayerControlled()` or controller class in pawn code; the SCL class-parity scan from Sprint 1 must stay green after every SCL change this sprint.

### Per-system coverage targets (`qa.level: full`)

"Tests" counts one automation test, selftest or CQTest scenario per story (every story names one test file), so the figures are lower bounds; the stories' QA cases hold the per-criterion cases. Report-gated and smoke-gated stories have no automated test.

**Estimated automated tests: about 135 across Must and Should and about 70 more in the Nice queue.**

### Where each story's cases come from

- **186 stories**: the story's own `## QA Test Cases` section is authoritative. Developers implement against it and add no cases during implementation. Shape example: PSR-014 AC-1 (each entering reason moves Active to Informant with the right pawn disposition; the Disconnect case needs the connection generation supplied or step 10 rejects it).
- **33 stories** have none: the next section derives them.
- **Edge-case themes the Must stories already require** (so reviewers can check nothing was under-tested): zero or minimum input (empty roster, `BeginMatch(5)` with no registrations, `UniformBelow(0)`, 0-byte SipHash message); boundary input (11th key rejected `Rejected_RosterFull`, the 4096th and 4097th log entry, `DueEpsilonMs` = 1 ordering, 63-byte SipHash message, `UniformInRange` span wrapping to 0); invalid or stale input (worker-thread mutation, client-side roster calls, old round epoch, unknown id, replaced controller); ordering and re-entrancy (FIFO events with strict `EventSeq`, depth-first follow-ons, cascade depth 9 logs `CascadeOverflow`).

## Test cases for stories that have none

These cases are derived **only** from each story's acceptance criterion and its QL-STORY-READY note. They are specs, not new behaviour. Where the QL note says the criterion is under-specified, the plan states the ruling needed; until the story author or qa-lead rules, the developer implements the narrowest reading shown and records the ruling in the story's completion notes. None of this changes an AC or a Status.

### Must Have

**PSR-001, Participant record fields equal the R3 whitelist exactly (Logic, `StealthGame.Roster.RecordSchemaWhitelist`)**
- Given the participant record type, when its fields are enumerated by the registered-field mechanism, then the set equals the exact name list in the test's constants file (per-record fields only; not the roster-wide counters MatchId, RoundEpoch, EventSeq; not the binding table), and no field name contains strike, defence, concealment or objective.
- Negative control: add one extra field to a copy of the fixture struct and show the test fails.
- RULING NEEDED (QL GAPS): the exact R3 field list and the enumeration mechanism for a pure-core struct with no UObject (`TFieldIterator` over a USTRUCT versus a registered field table).

**PSR-004, Every roster call on a client is rejected or answers not-targetable and faults (Logic, `StealthGame.Roster.ClientCallsRejected`)**
- Given authority = false, when each mutating call, `ResolveVictimKind`, `IsPawnBound`, `GetLegalityClass`, `CountActive`, `CountInformant`, `CountRoster` and `IsTeamEliminated` is invoked once, then: mutators with a result type return `Rejected_NotAuthority`; `ResolveVictimKind` returns `NotTargetable(Stale)`; `IsPawnBound` is false; counts are 0; exactly one fault is recorded per call (N calls, N faults); the store before and after is identical; no call returns `Npc` or a real count.
- RULING NEEDED (QL GAPS): a per-call expected-result table, including the client answer of `GetLegalityClass` and the result of mutators with no result type (`InvalidateAllBindings`, `RebindView`).

**PSR-009, Session connection states project onto Connection fields only (Logic, `StealthGame.Roster.ConnectionProjection`)**
- Given each projection delivered through `NotifyConnectionChanged`, then: only `Connection`, `DisconnectedAt` and `ConnectionGeneration` change; the generation rises by exactly 1 only on entry to `Disconnected`; the lifecycle state is unchanged; one `OnConnectionChanged` fires and consumes one `EventSeq`; a Lobby departure sets `Dormant`, keeps the id, and a later registration against a full roster ignores the Dormant record (`Rejected_RosterFull` does not count it).
- RULING NEEDED (QL GAPS): whether the R11 mapping lives in Roster (the call takes only the 3-value projection, so the Connecting and Rejected rows have no Roster behaviour) and whether a Disconnected-to-Disconnected move fires a second event. Until ruled, test only the 3-value projection and report the Connecting and Rejected rows NOT ASSESSED.

**IIF-001, Command and reply types match the ADR key interfaces (Logic, `StealthGame.Input.CommandReplyTypes`, `Source/StealthGameplay/Private/Tests/Input/CommandReplyTypesTest.cpp`)**
- Given the reflected enums and structs, when names, values and fields are enumerated, then `ECommandRejectCode` = {NotNow, Cooldown, Busy, OutOfReach}, `EHoldOutcome` = {Active, Completed, Cancelled}, `EActionType` = {Interact, Prepare, Attack, HideEnter, HideExit}, `ECancelReason` = {Released, Moved, Superseded, Illegal, OutOfRange, TargetInvalid, PawnRemoved, Reversed}, each `uint8`, contiguous from 0, with the exact counts asserted (4, 3, 5, 8).
- And `FClientCommandSeq` = {uint16 PossessionEpoch, uint32 Seq}; `FHoldStatus` = {Seq, ActionType, Outcome, double ServerStartTime, double ServerEndTime} with no cancel-reason field; `FCommandReply` = {Kind, Seq, Code, Hold}; `FNetPawnCommand` = {Kind, Seq, Args} with `Args` holding only ids and quantised values; no UObject-pointer field and no `ECancelReason` field in any reply or command struct.
- Edge: a ninth `ECancelReason` or a UObject pointer in `Args`, added to a fixture copy, fails the test.

**IIF-002, FPawnCommandCore runs headless with an injected clock and stub queue (Logic, `Source/StealthGameplay/Private/Tests/Input/PawnCommandCoreHeadlessTest.cpp`)**
- Given the core built with an injected clock and a stub queue and no UWorld, when `InteractBegin` is called, the clock advances 0.5 s and `InteractEnd` is called, then the stub queue holds exactly two items (Begin then End) with the given payload, every time read went through the injected clock (the spy counts reads; wall-clock reads = 0), and an include scan of the core's files finds no `UWorld`, `AActor`, `UActorComponent` or engine-time header.

**IIF-004, One batched ClientCommandReplies per connection per drain, null sink discards (Integration, `Source/StealthTestHarness/Private/ReplySinkDrainFlushTest.cpp`)**
- Given a drain where sink A holds 3 voided commands (queue keys 5, 2, 9), sink B holds 1 voided command and 1 `FHoldStatus`, and a null sink holds 2 voided commands, when the drain resolves, then the transport spy sees exactly one `ClientCommandReplies` for A (entries ordered 2, 5, 9) and one for B (ordered by key), each issued after the drain's last slot and none inside any slot; the null sink produces 0 calls and 0 buffered entries without error; a connection with an empty buffer at drain end receives no call.
- Sequencing: needs IIF-095's transport spy; build IIF-095 first or in the same batch.

**IIF-005, EntryPointSet (Logic, `Source/StealthGameplay/Private/Tests/Input/EntryPointSetTest.cpp`)**
- Given the command component, when its server entry points are listed by reflection, then they are exactly Move, Look, Traverse, Interact(Begin/End), Prepare(Begin/End), Attack and Hide(Enter/Exit); a fixture with one extra entry point fails the test.
- Note: IIF-094 places the production transport on the controller; the story author records which reflected class this test enumerates.

**IIF-006, NoCallerIdentityParameter (Logic, `Source/StealthGameplay/Private/Tests/Input/NoCallerIdentityParameterTest.cpp`)**
- Given every entry point, hub event and payload struct, when parameters and fields are reflected, then none has a type or name matching Controller, PlayerState, Team, IsAI or IsPlayer; and a grep of the component source for `IsPlayerControlled|IsLocallyControlled|IsNpc|GetTeam|NM_ListenServer` returns 0 hits.
- Negative control: plant each banned token once in a fixture file and show the grep reports it.

**IIF-094, Controller carries the command transport and client builder shell (Integration, `Source/StealthTestHarness/Private/ControllerTransportSkeletonTest.cpp`)**
- Given `AStealthPlayerController` and a possessed `AStealthPawn`, when `SetupInputComponent` runs and the class is reflected, then the `IA_*` actions are bound through `UEnhancedInputComponent`; `ServerPawnCommand(FNetPawnCommand)` is a reliable `WithValidation` Server RPC; `ClientCommandReplies` and `ClientSetPossessionEpoch` exist as reliable Client RPCs; `UPawnCommandClient` exists as a client-only component tracking outstanding Begins; and no gameplay RPC exists on `AStealthPawn` or its components (reflect every net-flagged function on the pawn class tree and assert zero).
- Evidence: a PIE check of the bindings after `SetupInputComponent`; a documented playtest only when the editor window is unavailable (D-3).

**IIF-095, Server command log, outgoing-RPC spy and stub doubles (Integration, `Source/StealthTestHarness/Private/CommandTestSeamsSelfTest.cpp`)**
- Given the harness module and a scripted command sequence, when the self-test runs it through the controller transport, then the server command log records each command's type, payload, `ClientCommandSeq` and arrival tick in script order; the outgoing-RPC hook records each client-to-server RPC and reports 0 for a sequence that sends none; each named stub double (Round queue, Roster legality class, SharedPawnStateView/Locomotion, Camera aim ray, Objectives interact-target owner, Assassination and Concealment predicates) records the calls made on it.
- Negative control: a script with one extra command changes both the log and the spy count.

**ST-006, PCG32 integer stream reproduces the reference outputs (Logic, `StealthGame.Random.Pcg32Vectors`)**
- Given `FIntStream` seeded as `pcg32_srandom_r(initstate 42, initseq 54)`, when the first outputs are drawn, then they equal the reference PCG32 outputs for that seed pair on every CI platform, using only `uint64`/`uint32` arithmetic with defined wrap, logical shifts, the rotation written `(32u - rot)` and `31u`, and no float.
- PROPOSED PIN (QL GAPS: "first outputs" has no count): fix the count at 6, the length of the `pcg-c-basic` reference demo listing for this seed pair; the implementer transcribes the six reference values into the test constants file from the reference source, never from this plan. Add a same-seed repeat (identical) and a different-seed-pair run (different).

**ST-007, UniformBelow, UniformInRange, WeightedPick and Fisher-Yates are unbiased and edge-safe (Logic, `StealthGame.Random.UniformBelowUnbiased`)**
- Given a fixed stream, when `UniformBelow(n)` is checked exhaustively for n up to 64 over a full 2^16-output window, then the per-residue counts match the Lemire multiply-shift expectation exactly (differ by at most 1 across residues); a chi-square test at a fixed named seed for n in {3, 24, 1000, 2^31-1} passes the threshold below; `UniformBelow(0)` is refused (returns 0 through the misuse branch and records a fault); `UniformInRange` of a span that wraps to 0 returns `NextU32()`; Fisher-Yates over a canonically sorted array is deterministic (same seed, same permutation).
- PROPOSED PINS (QL GAPS): chi-square critical value at p = 0.001 with df = n - 1, held as a named constant; the fixed seed and the stream behind the 2^16 window named in the constants file. Qa-lead accepts or revises these in the story before implementation.

**IIF-007, IA_* actions and IMC contexts exist and the trigger lint passes (Config/Data, `Source/StealthGameEditor/Private/Tests/InputAssetsAndTriggerLintTest.cpp`)**
- Given the assets under `Content/StealthGame/Input`, when the editor data lint runs, then `IA_Move` and `IA_Look` are Axis2D; `IA_WalkSlower` is Axis1D; `IA_Run`, `IA_Traverse`, `IA_Interact`, `IA_Prepare`, `IA_Attack`, `IA_Hide` are Boolean with no Hold, HoldAndRelease, Tap, Pulse or Chorded-action trigger on the action or any mapping of it; `IMC_Common` contains Move, Look, CameraToggle, ShoulderSwap, WalkSlower, Ping and menu; `IMC_Active` contains Run, Traverse, Interact, Prepare, Attack, Hide; `IMC_Informant` contains no gameplay action; no `UPlayerMappableInputConfig` asset or reference exists.
- Negative control: a temporary copy of one action with a Hold trigger must fail the lint (never modify a real asset).
- Asset hazard: new assets only; no existing `.uasset` is resaved (`production/never-resave-assets.md`). Evidence: smoke check pass in `production/qa/smoke-<date>.md`.

**ST-001, PIE harness hook forces client disconnect, rejoin, supersede and host kick (Integration, `StealthGame.Session.PIE.ConnectionEventHook`)**
- Given a PIE listen server with 2 or more clients, when the harness hook is called, then four CQTest methods each pass: (a) a chosen client's connection drops; (b) the same IdentityKey reconnects as a rejoin; (c) a second connection with the same key supersedes a live one; (d) the host kicks a chosen participant. No edit to the game code under test.
- PROPOSED PINS (QL GAPS: "deterministically" and which of (a)-(d) closes the spike): each method passes 10 of 10 consecutive runs; the spike closes PASS only when all four pass, otherwise FAIL plus the list of unsupported actions, reported in `production/qa/spikes/`. One time-boxed spike.

**ST-002, Net-emulation spike measures RTT, packet rate, burst outages and map load time (Integration, report-gated)**
- Given 3 clients on one machine under `StealthClean` and `StealthLeak1` (PktLag 100 ms, PktLoss 1 percent), when a 30-minute session (lobby phase, one round travel, an active round) runs per profile, then a report in `production/qa/spikes/` records R_c, the burst-outage distribution, RTT_p99, map load time t_load and server load T_srvload, and states for each of `SessionSoftTimeoutSec`, `SessionHardTimeoutSec`, `RejoinWindowSec`, `TravelLoadTimeoutSec`, `TravelAckGraceSec` whether the default is confirmed or revised.
- PROPOSED PINS (QL GAPS: no run-validity condition): a run is valid only if all 3 clients stay connected for the whole 30 minutes (otherwise the report records the abort and the run is repeated once); every capture is labelled development evidence (no 3060-class machine); each knob verdict names the measured value it rests on.

### Should Have

- RULING NEEDED (QL GAPS): the definition of "toggle setting" the scan matches on.

**IIF-019, D37: the sample's Ctrl jog toggle is removed (Integration, `Source/StealthTestHarness/Private/NoSampleCtrlToggleTest.cpp`)**
- Given a PIE character walking with W held, when Left Ctrl is pressed and released, then Gait value and speed are unchanged before and after the tap; and Ctrl held with W gives the 0.8 pace (112 cm/s at defaults).
- Dependency: IIF-017 (client scaling).

## Manual QA Checklist

Manual evidence in this sprint is spike reports, a few smoke records, one viewport screenshot gate, and PIE/multi-process runs that are only partly automatable. There is no UI. Evidence goes to `production/qa/evidence/` (screenshots, sign-off docs), `production/qa/spikes/` (spike reports) or `production/qa/smoke-<date>.md` (smoke records); a captured-and-discarded artefact is an assertion, not evidence.

### IIF-008 Spike V1: Enhanced Input edge behaviour on this project's contexts (Integration)
**Verification method**: spike report plus qa-lead review of the verdict (or the probe harness test `Source/StealthTestHarness/Private/SpikeV1EnhancedInputEdgesTest.cpp`)
**Who must sign off**: gameplay-programmer authors; qa-lead reviews the PASS/FAIL logic; technical-director only if FAIL or an ADR-0011 amendment request results
**Evidence to capture**: `production/qa/spikes/V1-enhanced-input-edges-report.md`
Checklist:
- [ ] The report names the engine build (5.8.4), the contexts (`IMC_Common`, `IMC_Active`), and the CVar value
- [ ] All six scenarios are present: plain press and release; context add while held; context remove while held with and without `bIgnoreAllPressedKeysUntilRelease`; window focus loss; menu open; the builder's outstanding-Begin flush
- [ ] Each scenario ran N times with N stated and per-scenario `Started`/`Completed`/`Canceled` counts tabulated
- [ ] Every scenario shows `Started` on press and exactly one terminal edge per release
- [ ] The builder flush yields exactly one End and no re-fired `Started`
- [ ] PASS or FAIL stated per scenario and overall; a FAIL names the fallback or amendment request

**Verification method**: spike report (multi-process or PIE with net emulation); needs the IIF-094 controller skeleton or direct Possess/UnPossess calls
**Who must sign off**: gameplay-programmer authors; qa-lead reviews

- [ ] Paths exercised: takeover, rejoin, same-pawn re-possession after an `Unresponsive` hand-over, `ClientRetryClientRestart`, null-pawn resend
- [ ] Each path ran with and without net emulation (PktLag 50 ms per direction, 1 percent loss)
- [ ] Per path: owner-side order of `ClientSetPossessionEpoch(N)` receipt, `ClientRestart` execution and `OwnerPossessionEpoch` at `ClientRestart`
- [ ] `ClientSetPossessionEpoch` precedes `ClientRestart` in every recorded run; any exception names the path and run

## Smoke Test Scope

Critical paths to verify before QA hand-off for Sprint 2 (run with `/smoke-check sprint`; the run is the developer's, this list is the scope):

1. The editor and the `StealthGame` module build clean; the editor launches the start map `L_Prototype` without a crash (no player-visible change is expected from this sprint, so a clean launch is the visible check).
2. The T0 lint and the per-commit gate pass (this sprint adds the TDC doc lint 029 to 037; any new lint failing the gate blocks hand-off).
3. All headless automation `^StealthGame.` passes, including the Sprint 1 suites (`Build`, `Harness`, `Locomotion.ClassParity`, `Locomotion.AnimBpNoLocalControlRead`) as the regression set.
4. Primary mechanics introduced this sprint, one pass each: Tuning pipeline (TDC-050 to 055 `Resolve()` with fallbacks and frozen set); Roster core (PSR-001 to 014); Round queue and Event Log (RMF-001 to 025); command core and controller transport (IIF-001 to 006, 094, 095); Session lifecycle (ST-014, ST-023) and RNG vectors (ST-005 to 008).
5. The CQTest listen-server-plus-clients PIE harness (`StealthGame.Harness.PIE.ListenServerThreeClients`) still passes after the IIF and ST changes touch the controller and game mode.
6. Regression risks from this sprint's changes: `AStealthGameMode` and `AStealthPlayerController` are new or changed (ST-023, IIF-094) and the sample's possession path must not regress; `Config/DefaultGame.ini` changes (TDC-057); new Content assets (TDC-056, IIF-007) must not have caused any existing asset to resave (`git diff --stat -- Content` shows only added files).
7. Save/load: not applicable (no save system exists yet; the Session stores are in-memory).
8. Performance: no budget applies to this sprint's Logic work; the Event Log stories (RMF-011 to 016) carry numeric size bounds that their tests assert. Any frame-time or memory number captured is labelled development evidence (no 3060-class machine).

## Playtest Requirements

| Story | Playtest goal | Min sessions | Target player type |
|-------|---------------|--------------|--------------------|
| IIF-018 (advisory) | Does holding Ctrl or Alt while walking feel like a controllable slow walk on keyboard, given the 0.8/0.9/0.8 scaling and the Alt-key OS side effects? | 1 (30 minutes, the designer) | experienced, keyboard |
| IIF-015 (advisory) | Are the default bindings reachable on keyboard/mouse and a gamepad without conflict? | 1 | new player |

Both are **advisory**, not mandated: the sprint's gate evidence for these stories is the CQTest result. They are flagged because the criterion language is partly subjective ("feel" of a walk modifier) and the QL note for IIF-018 asks for Alt behaviour to be recorded. If the user decides to run them, write the notes with `/playtest-report` to `production/qa/playtests/` naming the story. No other story in the sprint needs a playtest; the rest are Logic, report-gated spikes, or headless Integration.

**Sign-off requirement**: where a documented playtest stands in for an automated test under D-3, the playtest notes are written with `/playtest-report` to `production/qa/playtests/` (naming the story) and reviewed by the qa-lead before the story can be marked COMPLETE.

## Definition of Done: This Sprint

A story is DONE when ALL of the following are true (`qa.level: full`):

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified: via automated test result OR documented manual evidence (screenshot, spike report, or playtest notes with sign-off)
- [ ] Test file exists at the specified path for all Logic and Integration stories
- [ ] Every lint, scan and regression test has been **seen failing** against a planted violation or the unfixed code (negative control recorded)
- [ ] Spike stories close with a report in `production/qa/spikes/`: PASS, FAIL plus fallback, or an amendment request; never a skip
- [ ] Retained screenshot, in `production/qa/evidence/`, for CPA-003 and SCL-010 (and SCL-006 if pulled, per D-2); lead-signed frame sequence for IVP-005
- [ ] Signed-off evidence doc at `production/qa/evidence/[story-slug]-evidence.md` for CPA-003 (`test-character-import-evidence.md`)
- [ ] Smoke check passes (`/smoke-check sprint` before QA hand-off)
- [ ] No regressions: the Sprint 1 suites still pass; no existing `.uasset` or `.umap` resaved
- [ ] Zero unexpected faults at teardown in every automated test
- [ ] Code reviewed (via `/code-review` or documented peer review)
- [ ] Story file updated to `Status: Complete` (via `/story-done`)
- [ ] Sprint level: QA sign-off report APPROVED or APPROVED WITH CONDITIONS (`/team-qa sprint`); SCL-004's key-uniqueness clause closed by SCL-003 or carried again with a reason
